questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, which role lets users distribute Developer Sandboxes packs to non-production instances without full admin access?

explanation.correct: When the com.glide.dsb.licensing plugin is installed, the new sandbox admin role sn_dsb_commons.sandbox_license_admin lets users distribute sandbox packs to non-production instances without needing the full admin role. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-developersandboxes-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes name sn_dsb_commons.sandbox_license_admin, not this role, as the role for distributing sandbox packs.
This role is not named in the release notes; the documented role is sn_dsb_commons.sandbox_license_admin.
The release notes name sn_dsb_commons.sandbox_license_admin, not this role, as the sandbox pack distribution role.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Developer Sandboxes

source.excerpt: The new sandbox admin role (sn_dsb_commons.sandbox_license_admin) lets users distribute sandbox packs to non-production instances without full admin access.

questions.question: An administrator is setting up self-serve license assignment for Developer Sandboxes in the Brazil release. On which instance is the Developer Sandbox License Management (com.glide.dsb.licensing) plugin installed?

options.text: On each sandbox after it is allocated
On every production instance that hosts end users
On a personal developer instance used as a template

explanation.correct: The Brazil activation information says to install the Developer Sandbox License Management (com.glide.dsb.licensing) plugin on the license management instance, install the sandbox plugin on non-production instances, and use the license management UI in App Engine Management Center on the controller instance to distribute packs. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-developersandboxes-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes direct installing the licensing plugin on the license management instance, not on individual sandboxes.
The release notes direct installing the licensing plugin on the license management instance; packs are distributed to non-production instances.
The release notes do not mention personal developer instances in the licensing setup; the plugin goes on the license management instance.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Developer Sandboxes

source.excerpt: Install the Developer Sandbox License Management (com.glide.dsb.licensing) plugin on your license management instance.

questions.question: With the Brazil automatic update set sources feature for Developer Sandboxes, what happens when a new sandbox is created?

options.text: Update sets are automatically committed from the sandbox to production every 24 hours
An update set source pointing to the sandbox is created on the base instance, and one pointing to production is created on the sandbox
A single shared update set is created and locked for all sandboxes on the instance
The developer must manually create update set sources on both instances before transferring changes

explanation.correct: When a sandbox is created, an update set source pointing to the sandbox is automatically created on the base instance, and an update set source pointing to production is automatically created on the sandbox. When the sandbox is retired, both sources are removed automatically. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-developersandboxes-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes describe automatic creation of update set sources, not automatic commits on a schedule.
The release notes describe two update set sources being created, not a shared locked update set.
This option reverses the documented behavior: the update set sources are created automatically, without manual configuration.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Developer Sandboxes

source.excerpt: When a sandbox is created, an update set source pointing to the sandbox is automatically created on the base instance, and an update set source pointing to production is automatically created on the sandbox.

questions.question: Starting with the Australia release, which new role has the privilege to write checks on the scan_check table in Instance Scan?

explanation.correct: Instance Scan introduced the scan_check_writer role, which has the privilege to write checks on the scan_check table. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-instancescan-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes name scan_check_writer, not scan_admin, as the new role for writing checks.
The release notes name scan_check_writer, not scan_user, as the new role for writing checks.
This role is not named in the release notes; the new role is scan_check_writer.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Instance Scan

source.excerpt: Experience the new scan_check_writer role that has the privilege to write checks on the scan_check table.

questions.question: In the Australia release, a developer wants Instance Scan to execute scans on inactive checks. Which system property must be set to true?

explanation.correct: Scans can now run on inactive checks by setting the glide.scan.inactive_records property to true. A separate property, glide.scan.base_system_records, is added and enabled to execute scans on base system checks. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-instancescan-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes tie glide.scan.base_system_records to scanning base system checks, not inactive checks.
This property is not named in the release notes; inactive checks are controlled by glide.scan.inactive_records.
This property is not named in the release notes; inactive checks are controlled by glide.scan.inactive_records.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Instance Scan

source.excerpt: You can now execute scans on inactive checks by setting the glide.scan.inactive_records property to true.

questions.question: According to the Australia release notes, which ServiceNow SDK command transforms application metadata (XML) in the global scope on an instance into ServiceNow Fluent source code in a local global application?

explanation.correct: The ServiceNow SDK can move application metadata from the global scope into a global application: the now-sdk move command transforms global-scope metadata (XML) from an instance into ServiceNow Fluent source code so it can be customized in a local global application. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicenowsdk-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes name the now-sdk move command for this task, not now-sdk transform.
The release notes name the now-sdk move command for this task, not now-sdk convert.
The release notes name the now-sdk move command for this task, not now-sdk fetch.

references: Brazil delta release notes - ServiceNow SDK

source.excerpt: Transform application metadata (XML) in the global scope from an instance into ServiceNow Fluent source code ... using the now-sdk move command.

questions.question: According to the Australia release notes, in the ServiceNow SDK Access Control List API, which property on an ACL object controls whether someone can view or edit the ACL?

explanation.correct: The Access Control List API in the ServiceNow SDK supports protection policies: the protectionPolicy property in an ACL object controls whether someone can view or edit the access control list. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicenowsdk-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes describe readOnlyOption as a property of a Column object for read-only field options, not an ACL object property.
The release notes describe tableDefaultLanguage as a now.config.json parameter for field label language, not an ACL property.
This property is not named in the release notes; the ACL object property is protectionPolicy.

references: Brazil delta release notes - ServiceNow SDK

source.excerpt: Control whether someone can view or edit an access control list (ACL) with the protectionPolicy property in an ACL object.

questions.question: According to the Australia release notes, a developer wants to customize the directory structure used for metadata transformed into ServiceNow Fluent code. Where is this configured?

options.text: With the taxonomy parameter in the application's now.config.json file
With a system property in the sys_properties table on the instance
In the Package Manager user settings in the ServiceNow IDE
In the keys.ts file of the application

explanation.correct: The ServiceNow IDE lets you configure a custom directory structure for metadata transformed into ServiceNow Fluent code with the taxonomy parameter in an application's now.config.json file. By default, generated Fluent files are organized in a taxonomy-based structure within the fluent/generated directory. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicenowide-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes place this setting in now.config.json (the taxonomy parameter), not in a system property.
The release notes describe Package Manager user settings for configuring a private npm registry, not for the Fluent directory structure.
The release notes name the taxonomy parameter in the application's now.config.json file, not keys.ts, as the place to configure this directory structure.

references: Brazil delta release notes - ServiceNow IDE

source.excerpt: Configure a custom directory structure for metadata transformed into ServiceNow Fluent code with the taxonomy parameter in an application's now.config.json file.

questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, how does ServiceNow Studio display update sets and changes linked to source control?

options.text: Update sets appear on the Deployment tab while source control changes appear only in the Git CLI
Both display in the Changes tab, with support for using update sets and source control simultaneously
Source control replaces update sets, which can no longer be used in ServiceNow Studio
Each is shown in a separate color-coded tab grouped by scope

explanation.correct: In the Brazil release, update sets and changes linked to source control both display in the Changes tab of ServiceNow Studio, with clear tracking paths for both options and support for simultaneous update set and source control use. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicenowstudio-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes state both update sets and source control changes display in the Changes tab.
This option contradicts the release notes, which describe support for simultaneous update set and source control use.
The release notes state both display in the Changes tab; they also note integrated tabs are no longer color-coded or grouped by scope.

references: Brazil delta release notes - ServiceNow Studio

source.excerpt: Update sets and changes linked to source control both display in the Changes tab, with ... support for simultaneous update set and source control use.

questions.question: In the Brazil release, the Experience switcher has been removed from ServiceNow Studio. What do the release notes say about a replacement for it?

options.text: There is no current replacement, but each individual application can still be accessed on the ServiceNow AI Platform
It is replaced by the Tools tab on the ServiceNow Studio home page
It is replaced by the Create menu in the top right corner of ServiceNow Studio
It is replaced by a separate ServiceNow IDE application that must be installed from the ServiceNow Store

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes state the Tools tab was itself removed from the ServiceNow Studio home page, with no replacement.
The release notes state the Create menu in the top right corner of ServiceNow Studio has been removed.
The release notes say there is no current replacement for the Experience switcher; they do not describe a separate IDE application to install.

references: Brazil delta release notes - ServiceNow Studio

source.excerpt: There is no current replacement for the Experience switcher, but each individual application can still be accessed on the ServiceNow AI Platform.

The low-code wizard interface for creating tables

source.excerpt: The PDF Extractor tool that enables table creation from PDFs in App Engine Studio is deprecated starting in the Brazil release.

questions.question: Application Runtime Policy can be activated for an application in development in tracking mode or enforcing mode. Which statements correctly describe these modes? (Choose two.)

options.text: Tracking mode automatically approves generated policies

Enforcing mode automatically approves policies generated during testing

This option reverses the documented behavior: enforcing mode requires review and approval for each generated policy.
The release notes state Application Runtime Policy is a ServiceNow AI Platform feature that is active by default.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Application Runtime Policy

documentation.section: Application Runtime Policy - Brazil New features

source.excerpt: Tracking mode automatically approved generated policies, while enforcing mode requires review and approval for each generated policy.

questions.question: What does the Brazil ReleaseOps feature for creating a deployment request allow a team to do?

options.text: Skip all deployment assessments for hotfixes
Begin assessing deployment requests before creating or selecting a release
Deploy to on-premise and regulated environments
Merge multiple releases into a single deployment request automatically

explanation.correct: In Brazil, ReleaseOps lets you begin assessing deployment requests before having to create or select a release. Because some assessments take much longer than a release, starting them early speeds up time to deployment. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-releaseops-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes describe starting assessments earlier, not skipping them.
The release notes state ReleaseOps is not supported in regulated environments or on-premise.
The release notes do not describe merging releases; the feature lets assessments start before a release is created or selected.

references: Brazil delta release notes - ReleaseOps

source.excerpt: Begin assessing deployment requests before having to create or select a release.

The release notes list GlideElementDynamicAttributeStore as gaining new methods and being available by default, not as removed.
The release notes list GlideAggregate as gaining the new setAggregateWorkflow() method, not as removed.

questions.question: According to the Australia release notes, in UI Builder, what do event-driven UI Interactions replace?

options.text: Client scripts on Core UI forms
Declarative Actions using UXF Client Actions that required manual wiring on each page
Data resources bound to page controllers
Page variants used for audience targeting

explanation.correct: Previously, Declarative Actions using UXF Client Actions required manual wiring on each page, which led to complexity and upgrade risks. UI Interactions replace this with reusable, declarative event mapping, and can be applied across multiple events and pages. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-uibuilder-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes do not describe UI Interactions as replacing client scripts; they replace manually wired Declarative Actions using UXF Client Actions.
The release notes do not describe UI Interactions as replacing data resources or controllers.
The release notes do not mention page variants in connection with UI Interactions.

references: Brazil delta release notes - UI Builder

source.excerpt: Previously, Declarative Actions using UXF Client Actions required manual wiring on each page leading to complexity and upgrade risks. UI Interactions replace this with reusable, declarative event mapping.

documentation.section: Flows, subflows, and actions - Brazil New features

questions.question: According to the Australia release notes, how does Build Agent handle checkpoints and update sets?

options.text: Checkpoint 0 creates the base update set, and each later checkpoint creates its own update set
Checkpoint 0 no longer creates an update set, and Checkpoint 1 is the base update set for all subsequent changes
Checkpoints no longer use update sets; all changes go directly to source control
Every prompt creates a new update set named with the conversation ID

explanation.correct: Build Agent handles checkpoints and update sets differently: Checkpoint 0 no longer creates an update set, and Checkpoint 1 is the base update set for all subsequent changes. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-buildagentandautonomousengineer-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This option reverses the documented behavior: Checkpoint 0 no longer creates an update set, and Checkpoint 1 is the base update set.
The release notes state that Checkpoint 1 is the base update set, so update sets are still used.
The release notes state that Checkpoint 0 no longer creates an update set and Checkpoint 1 is the base update set for all subsequent changes; they do not describe a new update set per prompt.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Build Agent and Autonomous Engineer

documentation.section: Build Agent and Autonomous Engineer - Australia Changes

source.excerpt: Checkpoint 0 no longer creates an update set. Checkpoint 1 is the base update set for all subsequent changes.

questions.question: After upgrading to the Brazil release, an administrator wants ACLs to strictly deny access when none of the roles referenced in the ACL exist on the instance. What must be done?

options.text: Nothing; the behavior is on by default for upgraded instances
Remove all ACLs that reference a mix of valid and invalid roles

explanation.correct: Strict denial when none of the roles referenced in an ACL exist on the instance is on by default for new instances. On upgraded instances, use the glide.security.acl_with_invalid_roles_strict_deny property to turn it on. The behavior does not apply to ACLs with a mix of valid and invalid roles. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-accessmanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes state the behavior is on by default only for new instances; upgraded instances must turn on the property.
The release notes associate QueryRangeACLAuditor with generating query ACLs, not with strict denial for invalid roles.
The release notes state the strict denial behavior does not apply to ACLs with a mix of valid and invalid roles; removing them is not the documented step.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Access Management

source.excerpt: If you upgraded to this release, use the glide.security.acl_with_invalid_roles_strict_deny property to turn it on.
